name: Arterial Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Diagnostic Criteria for Arterial Thoracic Outlet Syndrome

criteria.description: Evidence of subclavian artery compression on imaging or angiography
Presence of upper limb ischemic symptoms such as claudication, pallor, or coldness
Positive provocative maneuvers reproducing symptoms or arterial flow obstruction
Exclusion of other causes of upper limb ischemia such as embolism or vasculitis

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of arterial compression on imaging plus ischemic symptoms in the affected limb
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis often requires combination of clinical, imaging, and exclusion of other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Subclavian artery compression with post-stenotic dilatation or aneurysm
searchTerms: artery narrowing with dilation or aneurysm

pathognomonic.symptomName: Upper limb ischemia manifesting as pallor and coldness
searchTerms: poor blood flow causing coldness and pallor

pathognomonic.symptomName: Claudication of the affected upper extremity

common.symptomName: Diminished or absent radial pulse on arm elevation
searchTerms: weak or missing wrist pulse when arm raised

common.symptomName: Arm fatigue or weakness during exertion
searchTerms: arm tiredness or weakness on use
fatigue in arm muscles during activity

common.symptomName: Neuropathic paresthesia due to nerve irritation
searchTerms: tingling or numbness from nerve irritation

common.symptomName: Cold intolerance of the affected limb
searchTerms: cold intolerance in arm or leg
blood clots causing blockage in small vessels
embolic events leading to poor blood flow

rare.symptomName: Muscle atrophy of the hand intrinsic muscles
searchTerms: muscle loss in hand intrinsic muscles
vascular spasm causing finger color changes

laboratory: Normal routine blood tests; inflammatory markers typically normal
Coagulation profile if embolic events suspected
imaging: Doppler ultrasound showing subclavian artery compression or flow obstruction
CT angiography or MR angiography demonstrating arterial stenosis, aneurysm, or post-stenotic dilatation
Conventional angiography as gold standard for diagnosis
other: Positive Adson’s test or other provocative maneuvers reproducing symptoms
Physical exam showing diminished pulses with arm positioning

distinguishingFeatures: Venous thrombosis and swelling predominant rather than arterial ischemia
Absence of arterial compression on imaging
Predominantly neurological symptoms without ischemic signs
Risk factors such as diabetes, smoking, hyperlipidemia

redFlags: Acute limb ischemia with pain, pallor, and pulselessness
Rapidly progressing digital ulceration or gangrene
Subclavian artery aneurysm rupture or embolization
references: Illig KA, Donahue D, Duncan A, et al. Thoracic outlet syndrome: a comprehensive review of pathophysiology, diagnosis, and treatment. J Vasc Surg. 2020;72(3):1022-1033.
Roos DB. Thoracic outlet syndrome: diagnosis and treatment. Muscle Nerve. 2017;56(3):345-356.
